parts.t: These are detached houses for sale in the City of Langley and the Township of Langley: one house on its own lot, at any price. Acreage and farms are left off so you can compare regular house lots side by side.

blocks.text: Why lot rules differ across Langley

parts.t: Langley is two municipalities, so a house lot follows either the City's rules or the Township's. Both updated their zoning in 2024 for the B.C. small-scale housing law, but they did it differently. That's worth knowing if you care about what you could add to a lot later.
The Township adopted its changes on November 18, 2024. According to its
small-scale housing page

, an eligible lot can have 3 units if it's 280 square metres or smaller, or 4 units if it's between 280 square metres and one acre. To be eligible, a lot must be inside the urban containment boundary, on both municipal water and sewer, not heritage-designated, and not in a Transit-Oriented Area.
That last group of conditions matters: a house on a well or septic doesn't qualify. Single family houses are still allowed in these zones either way.
Lot sizes also vary by plan. In Brookswood and Fernridge, the
Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan
sets minimum lots for its three single family areas at 2 acres, 10,000 square feet and 7,000 square feet.
In the City, most house lots are zoned RS1 or RS2. The City's
Zoning Bylaw
sets the RS1 minimum lot at 557 square metres, about 6,000 square feet, with a 16 metre width. A City
staff memo on Plex-Homes

says the average affected RS1 lot is 798 square metres and the average RS2 lot is 1,715 square metres. Both zones now allow a Plex-Home with up to 4 units, or 6 within 400 metres of a frequent bus stop.

Detached stock is spread across both cities, and lot sizes differ by plan area, as the Brookswood minimums above show. Langley City's 2021 plan counted 3,760 single detached units, with a total capacity of 3,046.

blocks.text: Checks before you write an offer

parts.t: Confirm which municipality the house is in. It changes the zoning, taxes and permits.
Ask whether the house is on city water and sewer, or a well and septic.
Pull the title for covenants and easements.
Look up permits for basements, decks and additions.
Get a home inspection, whatever the age of the house.

How many units are permitted on an eligible Township of Langley lot?
3 units for lots of 280 square metres or less, and 4 units for lots between 280 square metres and 4,050 square metres (1 acre). Lots larger than 1 acre are not eligible.
What's the minimum lot size in the City of Langley's RS1 zone?
557 square metres, about 6,000 square feet, with a 16 metre width.
Does this page include acreage or farms?
No. It shows detached houses on regular lots only.
What does a detached house cost in Langley?
FVREB publishes a monthly benchmark for a typical detached house in Langley, covering the City and the Township together. It's a modelled price, so individual houses sell above and below it.
